tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P1] Exchange invite fragments for tenant-bound admission transactions
tasks.description:
Replace reusable browser-side invite persistence with a qualified preflight exchange. Synchronously capture the HTTPS fragment and erase it before any asynchronous/network/analytics/third-party work, retain it only in ephemeral page memory for same-page retry, then create a ten-minute tenant/invite/cookie-bound admission and continue account or OAuth steps from the clean URL.

Acceptance criteria:
- A failed or hung first request still leaves the visible URL and current history entry clean before that request starts.
- The raw token never enters query strings, storage, cookies, logs, telemetry, DOM attributes, OAuth state, or connection records.
- Preflight validates tenant, issuer, lifecycle, expiry, revocation, use limit, and rate limit before safe preview.
- Invalid public cases share one non-oracular response.
- After successful exchange, reload uses only the HttpOnly pending transaction; another browser cannot replay it.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P1] Implement atomic join, reactivation, and channel-target redemption
tasks.description:
After authentication, atomically bind the pending admission to exactly one host account, then redeem without the raw token. Lock invite, tenant, account membership, and final-seat state; create, return, or reactivate one membership; optionally add one qualified channel; consume once per account; audit atomically; and retain a short-lived content-free consumed receipt for lost-response retry.

Acceptance criteria:
- A transaction cannot be rebound or redeemed by a different account, including an account switch in the same browser.
- New account, active member, and inactive member paths are idempotent and preserve immutable member identity.
- Reactivation revives no old grant, agent, credential, pairing, unrelated channel, or cursor.
- One final-seat race has one winner and no partial membership.
- A retry after committed redemption returns the same membership from the transaction/account receipt without reopening admission or consuming another use.
- Wrong-tenant and private-channel probes reveal nothing and mutate nothing.
- Account success followed by redemption failure is reported honestly and can retry while admission remains live.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P1] Scope leave, removal, sign-out, and credential revocation
tasks.description:
Make leave/removal tenant-scoped under DOR-2171, add recent-reauth and confirmation rules, block owner departure until DOR-2175 transfer, and expose separate browser sign-out and installation revocation operations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Leave/removal preserves the host account, browser sessions where specified, and every other membership.
- Selected-tenant channel memberships, grants, agents, credentials, and streams end atomically.
- Sign out ends only the current browser session; disconnect one/all revokes exactly the named installation grants.
- Owner leave cannot use host-operator authority as a bypass.
- Reactivation does not reverse earlier revocation.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P1] Complete tenant-bound installation pairing and disconnect status
tasks.description:
Connect each DorkOS installation only after membership through verifier-bound tenant pairing. Return authoritative per-grant status and distinguish revoked/disconnected from unavailable, including DOR-2191's error-classification contract.

Acceptance criteria:
- Approval names immutable community, installation label, requested scope, and expiry.
- No invite, host cookie, OAuth token, approval code, or grant enters a query/custom-protocol URL.
- Two installations receive independent grants and revocation.
- Revoked grants read as disconnected and protected routes deny them.
- Pairing and disconnect retries are idempotent and cross-tenant replay fails.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P2] Build host sign-in, chooser, and returning-member entry
tasks.description:
Implement host-root entry for unauthenticated, zero-, one-, and multi-membership accounts using only visible descriptors and canonical tenant routes. Handle archived, suspended, deletion-pending, removed, and stale last-selection states.

Acceptance criteria:
- No public directory or first-community fallback exists.
- One active membership enters directly; several show the chooser; zero show a clear empty state.
- Archived history remains reachable read-only; unavailable states route safely without host sign-out.
- Another browser needs account sign-in, not a new invitation.
- Routing and focus work at narrow widths and by keyboard.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P2] Build invitation review and account continuation
tasks.description:
Build the clean-URL invitation review, create/sign-in/OAuth continuation, safe expired/revoked recovery, idempotent completion, and channel-target confirmation. Lead with community/inviter facts and never redisplay or copy the raw token.

Acceptance criteria:
- The URL is clean before third-party content renders.
- Preview, account mode, OAuth return, redemption, and navigation survive reload from server state.
- Failure states say membership was not added and provide one safe recovery action.
- Existing active members do not create duplicate membership; inactive members see reactivation scope.
- Async updates are announced and focus remains coherent.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P2] Separate installation, session, channel, and membership controls
tasks.description:
Expose Connect this DorkOS installation, per-installation/all disconnect, browser sign-out, channel join/leave, and community leave as separate controls with exact scope summaries and server-authoritative status.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each action names what ends and what remains.
- Connection approval follows membership and cannot import a browser session.
- Disconnect never leaves; sign-out never disconnects; channel leave never leaves the community.
- Owner leave links through transfer then returns to the review.
- Removed/revoked state routes without false connected status.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P2] Distinguish host deployment from community creation and claim
tasks.description:
Build host-administration entry for later pending-owner creation and private owner claim while linking separately to the self-hosted deployment path. Keep role transition explicit when a host operator claims ownership.

Acceptance criteria:
- Create community cannot create provider resources; Deploy a new host cannot create a tenant on this host.
- Host authority alone never grants membership or content access.
- Idempotent creation, claim expiry/reissue, and claim handoff have reload-safe states.
- Pending communities never enter ordinary chooser or member routes.
- The first-host bootstrap remains one-time and visually distinct.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P3] Prove invitation, account, and cross-device security
tasks.description:
Exercise synchronous fragment erasure, failed/hung preflight, browser storage/log/telemetry absence, malformed lifecycle cases, account binding/switching, new/existing/inactive accounts, OAuth return, lost responses, concurrency, two browsers, two installations, and two hosts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated evidence finds no raw token in every forbidden sink and observes URL/history cleanup before a failed or hung request begins.
- Invalid invitation classes have equal public shape and zero side effects.
- Account-binding, final-seat, lost-response, reload, and retry races preserve one membership/use and never rebind the admission.
- Another device uses account sign-in while another installation requires independent approval.
- Cross-host and cross-tenant replay always fails without disclosure.

tasks.subject: [community-membership-journeys] [P3] Prove exact scope, accessibility, and standalone journeys
tasks.description:
Run the complete person journeys and assert exact effects for channel leave, browser sign-out, one/all installation disconnect, member leave/removal, owner transfer/leave, archived access, and post-action routing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every action's database, credential, stream, cache, and navigation effects match its scope summary.
- A1 actions leave A2 and host B unchanged.
- Owner departure is impossible before transfer and succeeds afterward without host sign-out.
- Keyboard, focus, announcements, narrow-width, offline/retry, and back/reload behavior pass.
- All journeys work with DorkOS Cloud unavailable.
